question:
DRAG DROP -
Drag and drop the mechanisms to collect data from a network from the left onto their characteristics on the right.
targets: Unstructured and susceptible to change and scripts failure.
It sends data from the device to a specific endpoint, for instance, JSON or by using Google protocol buffers.
It pushes messages in the format "seq no:timestamp: %facility-severity MNEMONIC:description" and has limits in scale and efficiency.
theory: Traditional network data-collection methods each carry well-known limitations that streaming telemetry was built to fix: CLI-based scripts scrape unstructured show-command text that breaks whenever output formatting changes; SNMP polls devices for MIB values but is typically limited to five-to-ten-minute polling intervals, too coarse for real-time troubleshooting; and syslog pushes free-form seq-no/timestamp/facility-severity messages that scale poorly. Model-driven streaming telemetry instead pushes structured data (JSON or Google Protocol Buffers) directly to a receiver as state changes occur, which is why each mechanism maps to its own distinct characteristic rather than sharing one description. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 6 — Traditional Monitoring Methods vs. Streaming Telemetry)
